llm_calls.reasoning: The alert is a fast burn on checkout's availability SLO (34.5% errors over 5m), and no other incidents are open. Checkout calls several services, so the root cause may be a downstream dependency; each investigator should start from checkout's client spans to find which dependency is failing.
Start by confirming checkout's error ratio onset and identifying which client span is erroring. Run the SLI range, the error client-span counts, and checkout's p95 latency in parallel.

Checkout's 1m error ratio is 1.0 from 15:44:35, and the only erroring client span is PaymentService/Charge (0.111/s). Next I'll check payment's own server-side error ratio, whether any other dependency is erroring, and the payment Charge client-span error ratio versus total calls, to see if payment is failing for everyone or only from checkout.

Checkout's 1m error ratio is 1.0 since 15:44:35, and the only erroring client span is PaymentService/Charge (0.111/s of 0.244/s, about 45%). Payment's own server spans show no error status (STATUS_CODE_UNSET only), so payment may not be the failing side. Next I need checkout's error messages and whether checkout changed recently, so I'll check its logs, rollout history, and flag state.

Checkout's PaymentService/Charge client spans began erroring at about 15:44:49, while payment's server spans show no error status, so the failure may be on the client side or in a path payment doesn't record as an error. Next I'll compare payment's server-side call counts by status, check the Charge client-span latency, and look for the Charge error rate on checkout over time.

Checkout's error ratio went to 1.0 at 15:44:35Z, and the only erroring client span is PaymentService/Charge. Payment's own server spans never recorded an error, and its traffic dropped to zero in the same window. I had no query budget left for rollout history, flags, logs or traces, so the root cause is not confirmed.
Start broad: checkout error logs and error traces around the onset, plus payment and cart logs to see which dependency is failing.

Checkout error logs are empty, but its error traces show every failure is a PaymentService/Charge dial timeout to 10.96.40.41:9999, and payment has no error-level logs. Next I'll read payment's unfiltered logs and traces, and search checkout's logs for the payment address.

Checkout's error traces all point to PaymentService/Charge dial timeouts to payment:9999, while payment shows no error logs or error traces. Payment's logs stop at 15:42:50, so I need to check whether payment received requests during the failure window, and whether checkout logged warnings. Next I'll query payment's most recent logs, checkout warnings, and payment error traces.

Checkout's error traces all fail on PaymentService/Charge with dial timeouts to 10.96.40.41:9999, and payment shows no error logs or error traces, with its last log at 15:42:50. Next I'll pull one failing trace to see where the time is spent, check checkout's Charge spans for timing, and look for payment-side warnings.

Checkout's error traces all trace back to PaymentService/Charge dial timeouts to payment:9999, while payment shows no errors in its own logs or traces. I did not check rollout history, flags, or Kafka, so the root cause is not confirmed. The next step would be to check payment's pod status and endpoints and the checkout rollout history.
Start broadly: checkout rollout history, flag state for all flags, and k8s events in otel-demo around onset. These are independent, so run them together.

Checkout revision 2 (15:42:52Z, change cause "payment client moved to port 9999") landed about 2.5 minutes before the alert, and all 18 flags are off. Next I'll diff revision 2 against revision 1 to confirm the port change, and check payment's rollout history and events to see whether it still listens on the old port.

Checkout revision 2 landed at 15:42:52Z, about 2.5 minutes before the alert, and its only change is PAYMENT_ADDR moving from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Payment has not changed since 15:30:15 and has no events showing a port change, so payment is probably still on its original port. My tools cannot query traces or metrics, so I can't confirm the checkout-to-payment error messages myself; I'll report the port mismatch as the likely cause and flag that confirmation as a hypothesis.

The checkout revision 2 config change (PAYMENT_ADDR payment:8080 to payment:9999) lines up with the onset, and checkout's own error traces show dials to payment's address timing out. Payment shows no errors and no restarts, so it is not the first failing service. Next step is to confirm the payment service's serving port and endpoints, then test a rollback to revision 1.

The diagnosis is well supported by cited rollout_history and deploy_diff results: checkout revision 2 (15:42:52Z) was the only change and altered PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999, and checkout's Charge errors are dial timeouts to 9999. Payment shows no faults and its traffic falls because checkout stopped reaching it. Rolling checkout back to revision 1 directly undoes the bad release, so I can propose it now without further checks.

result.report_summary: Checkout revision 2 (15:42:52Z, "payment client moved to port 9999") is the only recent change and fits the onset about 2.5 minutes before the alert. Its sole diff is PAYMENT_ADDR changing from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Payment has not been changed since 15:30:15, and no Kubernetes warnings show checkout or payment crashing. Checkout is the service showing the errors, and the likely cause is the misdirected payment address; this still needs trace confirmation.

Checkout's failures are all PaymentService/Charge calls that fail to dial payment:9999 (i/o timeout). Payment logs no errors and its last log is at 15:42:50, so the fault looks like unreachable payment rather than a payment-side exception. Root cause is not yet confirmed; payment pod health and the checkout rollout were not checked.

Checkout's availability burn is driven by its PaymentService/Charge client calls, which began failing at about 15:44:49Z and now fail on every call. Payment's server spans show no errors and its traffic falls to zero in the same window, while checkout's calls to payment return in about 2 ms. The failure looks like it sits between checkout and payment (unreachable payment, a bad address, or a failure before the payment span is recorded), not in payment's own handling. Checkout's own logs, rollout history and flags were not checked.

actions.reason: Revision 2 (15:42:52Z), the only change in the window, set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999. Checkout Charge errors are 'dial tcp 10.96.40.41:9999: i/o timeout'. Reverting to revision 1 restores payment:8080.

alternatives.why_not: A restart would reload the same bad PAYMENT_ADDR config and would not fix the failures.
Checkout is not short of capacity. Its failures are fast dial errors, not overload.
Leaving it in place keeps about a third of checkout orders failing and burns the error budget at fast-burn rate, so a fix is warranted.

plan.summary: Checkout revision 2 pointed PAYMENT_ADDR at payment:9999, which nothing listens on, so every Charge call times out and about 34% of checkout requests fail. Rolling checkout back to revision 1 restores payment:8080 and should bring the error ratio back to baseline within a few minutes, after which payment traffic and frontend errors should recover.

facts.statement: Checkout revision 2 was created at 15:42:52Z and was the only change. Its diff changes only PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999.
All checkout error spans are PaymentService/Charge or PlaceOrder failures with 'dial tcp 10.96.40.41:9999: i/o timeout'.
Payment has one revision from 15:30:15Z, shows no restarts or warnings, and has no error or warn logs. Its last log is at 15:42:50.
Payment's server spans have no error series. Its Charge rate drops to zero by 15:45:49Z.
Checkout's Charge client spans are STATUS_CODE_ERROR at about 0.24-0.27 calls/s from about 15:44:49Z, and checkout's Charge p95 is about 1.9 ms, so failures are fast and not timeouts.
Kubernetes warnings over 120 minutes are only readiness probes on alertmanager, otel-collector-agent and loki. None involve checkout or payment.
Frontend server errors are 0.4-0.6/s from 15:44, while cart, currency, shipping, email, product-catalog and kafka show no server-side errors.

hypotheses.statement: Payment serves only on 8080, so nothing listens on 9999.

inferences.statement: The 9999 address change caused checkout's failures. The 2.5-minute gap to the error onset at 15:44:35 is consistent with pods rolling and the metrics lag.
Payment is a victim, not the cause. Its traffic falls to zero because checkout no longer reaches it.
Frontend's errors are a symptom of checkout failing, and flags, Kafka and checkout resource pressure are unlikely.

root_causes.cause: Config release revision 2 set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999, but payment serves on 8080, so every Charge dial times out and checkout fails about 34% of requests. Fix by reverting PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080 or rolling back to revision 1.

Payment being unreachable or broken. Considered and judged unlikely: payment has no errors, no restarts, and its last log is at 15:42:50, which matches checkout's config change rather than a payment fault.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's availability burn comes from its PaymentService/Charge calls failing on every attempt. Checkout revision 2 (15:42:52Z) changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999, the only change in the window. Checkout's error traces show 'dial tcp 10.96.40.41:9999: i/o timeout'. Payment has no errors, no restarts, and no changes since 15:30, and its traffic drops to zero. Checkout is the service to fix: revert PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080 (rollback to revision 1). Flags and Kafka are ruled out.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Checkout revision 2, created 2026-10-28T15:42:52Z, is the current revision and was the only change, with change cause "checkout config release: payment client moved to port 9999". Revision 1 dates from 15:30:16Z.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: The diff between checkout revision 1 and 2 changes exactly one thing: container env PAYMENT_ADDR goes from payment:8080 to payment:9999.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Payment has one revision (1, created 15:30:15Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-payment) and its pod started normally at 15:30:31Z with no restarts or warnings. Nothing shows payment changing to listen on port 9999.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Checkout's config change moved the payment address to port 9999 about 2.5 minutes before the alert opened (15:45:18Z), and the 34.5% error rate fits a checkout-to-payment connection failure. The likely cause is that checkout now dials a port payment does not serve. This is an inference that still needs checkout's client spans or logs showing connection errors to payment:9999.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: All 18 feature flags in flagd are off, so no fault-injection flag explains the failures.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Kubernetes warnings in otel-demo over the last 120 minutes are only readiness-probe failures on alertmanager, otel-collector-agent and loki, all around 15:30. None involve checkout or payment, so checkout is not crash-looping or OOM-killed.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Hypothesis: reverting checkout's PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080 (rollback to revision 1) should restore checkout's availability. Confirm by checking that checkout's client spans to payment stop erroring after the rollback.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: checkout service:sli_error_ratio:rate1m is 1.0 from 2026-10-28T15:44:35Z through 15:45:35Z (checkout's error onset).

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Of checkout's client spans, only oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge is erroring: about 0.111 error calls/s over 5m, and checkout's PlaceOrder server spans show 0.124 error calls/s.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: From about 15:44:49Z, checkout's Charge client spans are STATUS_CODE_ERROR at about 0.24-0.27 calls/s, and the UNSET series drops to 0 by 15:45:49Z. Every Charge call is failing in the latest minutes.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Payment's server spans have no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series at all. Its Charge server-span rate falls from about 0.2-0.4/s to 0 by 15:45:49Z, and the payment error-ratio series has no data in the window.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Checkout's p95 latency to PaymentService/Charge is about 1.9 ms in the latest minutes (31 ms at onset, then about 3.9-7 ms). Checkout's overall p95 is 47.12 ms. The Charge failures are fast, not timeouts.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Inference: payment is not the first failing service. Its server spans show no errors, and checkout's Charge calls fail quickly while payment records nothing, so the fault is most likely on the checkout-to-payment path (network, address/config, or payment unavailable before instrumentation). Confirming needs checkout logs for the Charge error message and payment pod status.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Frontend server spans show 0.4-0.6 error calls/s from 15:44 onward, while cart, currency, shipping, email, product-catalog and kafka show no server-side error series. Frontend is a symptom of checkout's failure, not a separate cause.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Not checked: checkout and payment Deployment rollout history, flagd state, Loki logs and Jaeger exception messages. Hypotheses 2-5 (a bad checkout rollout, a fault-injection flag, Kafka, or checkout resource pressure) remain open.
